newsitem.title: USA: Stocks mixed after sell-off on latest jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks mixed after sell-off on latest jobs data.

text.p: Stock prices were slightly mixed Thursday after rebounding from a sell-off triggered by stronger-than-expected labour data for the latest week.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was down 4.10 points at 5,926.52, after losing 25 points initially.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on volume of 232 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow index was under selling pressure this morning following news that jobless claims posted a surprisingly sharp drop last week.
The report, which showed new jobless claims falling to 319,000 from a revised 341,000 in the prior week, rekindled concerns about wage-driven inflation.
The inflation-sensitive Treasury market slipped, with the 30-year Treasury bond off 13/32, boosting its yield to 6.86 percent from 6.83 at Wednesday's close.
Despite bonds' inability to shake their losses, stocks recovered as investors shrugged off the weekly numbers and returned their focus to earnings.
"At this point the market is going to stay in a pretty tight range until next week, when we start to see earnings," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management.
"Technology earnings are going to be key because they've been leading the market," he said.
Investor enthusiasm for large technology companies like Microsoft Corp. and Intel Corp. helped lift the Nasdaq Composite index, which gained 4.32 points at 1,242.30.
Altera Corp., another high technology firm, jumped 5-5/8 to 59-1/2 after reporting stronger-than-expected earnings.

"The techs and semiconductors continue to act very well," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We continue to see significant buying (in techs) on any signs of weakness."
Even some recently out-of-favour computer industry names, like Apple Computer Inc. rallied. Apple was up 1-3/8 to 24-3/8 after Prudential Securities upgraded the shares.
Among other issues, Olin Corp. surged 3-3/4 to 87-7/8 after the company announced a series of restructuring measures, including plans to spin off its ordnance and aerospace units.
Olin also said it would sell its isocyanates business to ARCO Chemical Co. for $565 million. ARCO Chemical was unchanged at 49-1/8.
Sunglass Hut International Inc. skidded 4-3/8 to 9-1/8 after warning that its third quarter earnings would fall below year-ago levels.
